title: A Number With No Exact Fraction

steps.body: Draw a square with side length 1. Its diagonal has length c, where 1² + 1² = c² (the Pythagorean theorem), so c² = 2. No fraction, when squared, lands on exactly 2 — this diagonal's length is called an **irrational number**, written √2.

widget.prompt: Since c² = 2, which best describes c?

choices.label: c = √2, and no fraction squares to exactly 2
choices.feedback: Right — √2 is irrational precisely because no a/b squares to 2 exactly.

choices.label: c = 1.5, since 1.5² = 2.25 ≈ 2
choices.feedback: 1.5² = 2.25, which is close but not exactly 2 — no decimal or fraction hits 2 exactly.

choices.label: c = 1, since a square's diagonal equals its side
choices.feedback: The diagonal is always LONGER than the side — c must be bigger than 1.

choices.label: c can't exist as a number
choices.feedback: It exists — it's just not a rational number. √2 ≈ 1.41421… sits right there on the number line.

steps.body: Compare with √4: since 4 = 2², √4 = 2 exactly — a whole number, so it's rational. But √2, √3, √5, and √7 are irrational, because none of 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, … (the perfect squares) equals 2, 3, 5, or 7.
Which of these IS rational (a perfect square root)?
explanationVariants: √16 = 4 exactly, since 16 = 4² is a perfect square.
16 is on the perfect-square list (1,4,9,16,25,…), so its root is a whole number.

choices.feedback: Right — 16 = 4², so √16 = 4 exactly.
10 isn't a perfect square — no whole number squares to 10.
20 isn't a perfect square either — it's between 4²=16 and 5²=25.
2 isn't a perfect square — this is the classic irrational example.

explanationVariants: 50 sits strictly between 49=7² and 64=8², so it's not a perfect square — √50 is irrational.
No whole number squares to exactly 50, which is exactly what makes a square root irrational.

choices.label: Irrational, since 50 isn't a perfect square
choices.feedback: Right — 50 sits between 7²=49 and 8²=64, never landing exactly.

choices.label: Rational, since 50 is even
choices.feedback: Being even doesn't matter — what matters is whether 50 is a PERFECT square, and it isn't.

steps.body: Irrational numbers have no exact fraction — √2 is the classic example.
takeaways: √2 is the diagonal of a unit square, and no fraction squares to exactly 2.
Perfect-square roots (√4, √9, √16, …) are the rational exception.
A root is irrational exactly when its radicand isn't a perfect square.

concept.body: A square root is rational only when its radicand is a perfect square (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …); otherwise it's irrational.
